dataset_card.name: TCGA-BRCA diagnostic slides with clinical variables
dataset_card.description: Breast cancer patients with H&E whole-slide images and six clinical variables: age, stage, histological type, and the receptor statuses ER, PR and HER2 from immunohistochemistry. Images are represented by frozen pathology foundation models: five encoders, each giving one feature vector per tile (up to 128 tiles per slide, identical tile positions across encoders) and a mean-pooled vector per patient. The label is the PAM50 intrinsic subtype in four classes. Patients without a label still have images. Each patient has a collection site.

label_provenance.statement: PAM50 is computed from the tumour's RNA expression. Receptor status is correlated with PAM50 but is a separate clinical measurement and is not equivalent to it (immunohistochemistry surrogates disagree with PAM50 for a substantial share of tumours).
label_provenance.implication: No RNA-derived variable may be used as an input. Whether receptors may be used depends on the question asked: they are a legitimate baseline when the question is what images add to clinical information, and a forbidden shortcut when the question is what images alone contain.

dataset_card.scope_of_inference: incremental predictive value in this cohort; not an independent biological mechanism
dataset_card.how_predictions_are_scored: The evaluator re-runs every method inside its own repeated nested cross-validation on the labelled patients (outer 5 folds repeated 3 times, patient-level; any model or configuration choice happens only inside the training folds) and compares it with a fixed, fully tuned clinical-only model on the same patients and folds.

rulers.floor_clinical: clinical variables only, fixed and fully tuned by the evaluator; the gain is measured against it
rulers.simple_reference: clinical variables plus mean-pooled image features in a logistic regression; complex methods are compared with it
rulers.historical_reference: an earlier project's late fusion reached macro-F1 0.723 on a single 121-patient test split (not ground truth)

dataset_card.decision_rule: Primary metric: paired difference in macro-F1 (image plus clinical minus clinical only) with a patient-level bootstrap 95% interval. Conclusion, from the interval alone: "improves" if the lower bound is above 0; "insufficient evidence" if the interval contains 0; "worse" if the upper bound is below 0. Secondary: log-loss difference, one-vs-rest AUROC difference, per-class recall changes (LumA and LumB in particular), and a site-held-out sensitivity analysis. Both arms must use the same patients and the same missing-value handling.
dataset_card.deliverable: The estimated gain with its interval, the three-way conclusion, out-of-fold predictions for both arms, and the per-class changes.

difficulties.evidence: Class counts among 802 labelled patients: LumA 410, LumB 190, Basal 137, Her2 65. The smallest class is 8.1% of the cohort.
difficulties.implication: Use a class-balanced metric and class weighting; an unweighted model can score well while missing the smallest class entirely.

difficulties.evidence: Share of labelled patients without a definite value: er 4.7% (missing 4.5%), pr 5.1% (missing 4.6%), her2 31.8% (missing 15.3%), stage 2.6% (missing 2.6%), histological_type 0.1% (missing 0.1%), age 0.0% (missing 0.0%).
difficulties.implication: Handle missing values inside each training fold with an explicit missing level, identically in both comparison arms.

difficulties.evidence: 802 labelled patients against image features of 1536 (UNI2-h), 768 (CONCH-Z), 2560 (Virchow2), 1024 (MUSK), 1536 (H-Optimus-1) dimensions per encoder.
difficulties.implication: High-capacity image models overfit easily; regularise, reduce dimension inside folds, and require evidence of convergence and of a gain over a simple reference.

difficulties.evidence: Labelled patients come from 19 collection sites (largest 130 patients, 3 sites with fewer than 10). Image features (UNI2-h) identify the site of a patient with accuracy 0.89 against 0.17 for always guessing the largest site; site and class are associated (Cramer's V = 0.21).
difficulties.implication: Part of an image-based gain may come from site signatures; a site-held-out sensitivity analysis should accompany the main estimate.

difficulties.evidence: PAM50 is computed from the tumour's RNA expression. Receptor status is correlated with PAM50 but is a separate clinical measurement and is not equivalent to it (immunohistochemistry surrogates disagree with PAM50 for a substantial share of tumours).
difficulties.implication: No RNA-derived variable may be used as an input. Whether receptors may be used depends on the question asked: they are a legitimate baseline when the question is what images add to clinical information, and a forbidden shortcut when the question is what images alone contain.

difficulties.evidence: 46 labelled patients have more than one slide; tiles per patient range from 6 to 471 (median 124).
difficulties.implication: The patient is the unit of analysis: all slides and tiles of a patient must stay on the same side of every split.

difficulties.evidence: Clinical variables alone reach macro-F1 0.576 in 5-fold cross-validation; recall by class: LumA 0.54, LumB 0.54, Basal 0.82, Her2 0.52. The weakest class is Her2.
difficulties.implication: The question is about what images add to this baseline, so the clinical arm must be tuned as carefully as the image arm and evaluated on the same patients.

difficulties.evidence: For a simple image-plus-clinical model against clinical only, the paired macro-F1 difference has a bootstrap standard error of 0.021 with one 5-fold split of 802 patients. The smallest difference detectable with 80% power is about 0.059.
difficulties.implication: Gains of a few points cannot be established from one split; use repeated cross-validation and report an interval, not only a point estimate.

difficulties.evidence: 5 image encoders are available, each usable at tile or patient level with several fusion strategies.
difficulties.implication: Choosing the best of many configurations on the evaluation folds inflates the reported gain; selection must be nested or counted.
